stem: A frequency distribution has classes 10-20, 20-30, 30-40, 40-50, and 50-60. Each class is of the form [lower limit, upper limit). The class width for every class in this distribution is:

per_option_rationale.rationale: Class width = upper limit - lower limit = 20 - 10 = 10, uniform across all five classes.
Halving the class width by mistake, perhaps dividing the range of the full distribution by the number of classes times 2.
Reading the span of three consecutive limits (10 to 25) instead of a single class boundary difference.
Confusing class width with the span of two classes, giving 40 - 20 = 20.

explanation: Class width is simply upper class limit minus lower class limit. For 10-20 that is 20 - 10 = 10, and this holds for every class here since the distribution has equal class widths.

explanation_sections.punchline: Equal class width = upper limit - lower limit = 10 for every class.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: this is a uniform-width frequency distribution. The decisive move is computing upper minus lower for any single class. For 10-20: 20 - 10 = 10. Verify with 20-30: 30 - 20 = 10. All classes confirm 10.
explanation_sections.lesson: Class width is always upper limit minus lower limit for a single class, not the range of the entire distribution.
explanation_sections.timing: 10 seconds. No calculation required beyond simple subtraction. Trap: do not divide total range (60-10=50) by number of classes (5) and get 10 that way - it happens to match here but is not the definition.
